newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Tower Corp positive on demutualisation - paper.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Tower Corp positive on demutualisation - paper.

text.p: Tower Corporation is moving from a passive to an active position on demutualisation, the Dominion newspaper reported on Monday.
Chairman Colin Beyer said the former Government Life was the last of the main superannuation and insurance mutual societies in Australia and New Zealand to deal with demutualisation.
AMP, Colonial Mutual and National Mutual had all either demutualised or were in the process.
Beyer said any decision to demutualise was ultimately in the hands of policyholders.
"But it's looking like something that would be desirable from the point of view of all policyholders," he said.
"It would be of great benefit to them. We've seen some other examples of this recently of course."
Policyholders would benefit because they would become owners of something they own "theoretically" now, Beyer told the Dominion.

"They'll have some ability to trade it if they want to or just enjoy dividends from it, and they'll have a very good insurance contract with our company. So they're getting the best of both worlds by that sort of dichotomy," he said.
The process of demutualisation would take about two and a half years. Beyer said it would be better to go slowly than to rush it "in the way that some of the power companies have done".
Demutualisation would need at least 75 per cent approval from Tower's more than 400,000 policyholders in New Zealand, Australia and the Pacific.

In the past Tower had taken a "softly, softly" approach to demutualisation, though Beyer said the group's directors would be failing in their duties not to consider the merits of various ownership structures.

Demutualisation as a way for Tower to raise funds to invest in new businesses or to make up for a shortage of available capital was not relevant to Tower, Beyer told policyholders at the 1995 annual meeting.
In the past year Tower bought Adelaide-based Austrust for an undisclosed sum.
Beyer became chairman of Tower in 1990 and is standing again for selection at the annual meeting in February.
